reason: E2 supports that gas nitriding of AISI H13 improves wear/corrosion resistance at high temperatures, and E3 supports that PVD coatings like TiSiN and AlCrN retain hardness and oxidation resistance up to 500 °C. However, no cited evidence demonstrates the specific multilayer combination (TiSiN/AlCrN) on nitrided H13, the claimed adhesion enhancement from the nitrided interlayer, or the quantitative 50% hardness increase and 5× wear reduction.
premises: Gas nitriding of AISI H13 forms a hard surface layer that improves wear and corrosion resistance at elevated temperatures
PVD ceramic coatings (e.g., TiSiN, AlCrN) provide high hardness, oxidation resistance, and thermal stability up to at least 500 °C
A nitrided diffusion layer can act as a graded transition to enhance adhesion of a subsequently applied PVD coating
The combination of nitriding and a multilayer PVD coating yields a ~50% hardness increase and ~5× wear rate reduction versus untreated H13
These benefits persist under aggressive conditions up to 500 °C with abrasive and corrosive loading
